citation: Cao, Fatemi, Fang, Watanabe, Taniguchi, Kaxiras & Jarillo-Herrero, "Magic-angle graphene superlattices: a new platform for unconventional superconductivity", Nature 556, 43 (2018); arXiv:1803.02342v2
license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license; facts and numbers only, no text or figures reproduced
topic: The superconducting state of an atomically thin MA-TBG device (Tc about 0.5 K) was suppressed with magnetic fields perpendicular and parallel to the layers.

facts.text: The twisted bilayer is about 0.6 nm thick.
The perpendicular critical field gives a Ginzburg-Landau coherence length of about 52 nm.
The in-plane critical field extrapolates to about 1.1 T at T = 0.
For this Tc the BCS Pauli (paramagnetic) limit, 1.85 T/K × Tc, is about 0.93 T.

ask: Estimate the in-plane critical field that orbital (Ginzburg-Landau thin-film) pair breaking would give for this thickness and coherence length, and compare it with the measurement. Choose the option in which both the value and the conclusion are correct.

error.reason: 套用垂直场的 GL 公式 Φ0/(2πξ²)，忽略了平行场下轨道效应受膜厚 d 限制。

paper.text: The orbital limit is far above the measured 1.1 T, which lies close to the Pauli limit: in-plane superconductivity is destroyed by Zeeman (paramagnetic) pair breaking, not by orbital currents.
paper.locator: Magnetic field response (p. 5): d ≈ 0.6 nm would imply ~36 T; dependence interpreted as paramagnetic pair breaking

rejected.text: The measured 1.1 T is set by orbital pair breaking: the in-plane field destroys superconductivity through screening currents in the bilayer.
rejected.reason: 原文指出原子级厚度使轨道极限约 36 T，远高于实测，因而排除轨道机制。

scale.definition: 双层厚度 d（与 ξ 比较决定平行场轨道极限）
